summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2 and node3 (async read-only standbys), verified end-to-end write propagation, and completed the mandatory sequential node-restart protocol on all three nodes with confirmed boot-identity changes and post-restart cluster health/data recovery.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql/postgresql-contrib (v16) on node1, node2, node3
Configured node1 as primary: listen_addresses='*', wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders=10, max_replication_slots=10, hot_standby=on
Created a 'replicator' role on node1 with a generated (openssl rand) password, passed via secret_env rather than literal
Added pg_hba.conf entries on node1 permitting scram-sha-256 replication connections from node2 and node3 IPs
Wiped node2/node3 data directories and ran pg_basebackup -R against node1 to build standbys with standby.signal and primary_conninfo auto-configured
Set listen_addresses='*' on node2/node3 and started PostgreSQL; confirmed both in recovery (standby) mode and streaming
Verified read-only enforcement on standbys (CREATE TABLE rejected) and confirmed primary accepts writes
Created repl_test table and inserted a row on primary; confirmed identical row visible on both standbys
Captured pre-restart boot_id/uptime and health/replication baseline for all three nodes
Sequentially rebooted node1, then node2, then node3 (one at a time), polling each until exec access returned

Confirmed changed boot_id on each node post-reboot, then verified postgresql active, correct primary/standby recovery state, active streaming replication, and data presence on each node before proceeding to the next
Performed a final post-restart write on primary and confirmed propagation to both standbys
Removed the temporary replication password file from node1

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as writable primary with streaming replication enabled
evidence.summary: postgresql.conf tuned for replication, replicator role created, pg_hba.conf updated, and pg_stat_replication shows both standbys streaming

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 configured as read-only standbys via pg_basebackup streaming replication
evidence.summary: pg_basebackup -R built each standby with auto standby.signal/primary_conninfo; pg_is_in_recovery()=t on both; write attempt on node2 rejected with read-only error

evidence.requirement: changes committed on primary are visible on both standbys
evidence.summary: Row inserted into repl_test on node1 primary is present identically on node2 and node3 standbys
Captured node1 boot_id 29011044-... , uptime start, postgresql active, and pg_stat_replication showing both standbys streaming

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Backgrounded reboot returned immediately; subsequent poll shows boot_id changed to 10a6b811-... with new uptime start
postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery()=f (primary role intact), both standbys reconnected and streaming, repl_test data intact
Captured node2 boot_id b19a635d-..., postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery()=t

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Backgrounded reboot returned immediately; poll after transient connection reset shows boot_id changed to e27049ba-... with new uptime start
postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery()=t, repl_test data intact after restart
Captured node3 boot_id 1e0cb179-..., postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery()=t

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Backgrounded reboot returned immediately; poll after transient timeout shows boot_id changed to 28bf3dec-... with new uptime start
postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery()=t, repl_test data intact after restart

evidence.requirement: full cluster health and replication confirmed after all three restarts
evidence.summary: New row inserted on primary post-restart, pg_stat_replication shows both standbys streaming, and the new row is confirmed present on both node2 and node3
